title: Indian American Teen Kiran Reddy Crowned Miss Teen USA 2026, Makes History for Georgia
excerpt: The 18-year-old from Douglas, Georgia, becomes the first Indian American and the first Georgian to win the Miss Teen USA title.
body:
• Kiran Reddy, 18, won the Miss Teen USA 2026 crown on August 26 in Miami, becoming the first Indian American and the first contestant from Georgia to win the title.
  • Reddy, a valedictorian from Coffee High School in Douglas, Georgia, plans to study biology on a pre-med track at the University of Georgia this fall with ambitions in women's health.
  • She will represent the United States at Miss Teen Universe in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, in October 2026.
  • Reddy first made history in July when she became the first Indian American to win Miss Georgia Teen USA through an open casting call.

Kiran Reddy, an 18-year-old from Douglas, Georgia, was crowned Miss Teen USA 2026 on August 26 at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts in Miami, defeating 50 other contestants in the 44th edition of the pageant.

The win marks a double milestone: Reddy is the first Indian American to claim the national title and the first contestant from Georgia to win Miss Teen USA in the pageant's four-decade history.

From Small-Town Georgia to a National Stage

Reddy's path to the crown began in July 2026, when she was appointed Miss Georgia Teen USA through the pageant's open casting call, becoming the first Indian American to hold the state title. She had placed first runner-up at the 2024 state competition and second runner-up in 2025 before breaking through.

"I am so excited and blessed to represent Georgia and the U.S. and be the role model I always needed growing up."

— Kiran Reddy, Miss Teen USA 2026

The daughter of a physician, Reddy graduated as valedictorian of Coffee High School's Class of 2026. She plans to enroll at the University of Georgia this fall on a pre-med track, with ambitions to specialize in obstetrics and gynecology. Her interest in women's health deepened while volunteering in the labor and delivery wing of Coffee Regional Medical Center.

A Night of Historic Firsts

Reddy's crowning was part of a broader evening of firsts at the Miss USA pageant. In the main competition held the following night, Justus Kelley of Virginia became the first married woman and first mother to win Miss USA, following rule changes introduced in 2023 that removed the age cap and restrictions on married contestants.

In the teen division, Raquel Olea of Arkansas was named first runner-up, while Elisa Akin of New York, Kiersten Alvarado of Indiana, and Chloe Bella Dietz of Texas completed the top five. The event was hosted by former Miss USA 2023 Noelia Voigt and model Sean Michael Rae. Last year's winner, Mailyn Marsh of Missouri, placed the crown on Reddy.

Community Service and Aspirations

Beyond academics and pageantry, Reddy has built a record of community engagement. She has volunteered at local elementary schools, served residents of Lakeside Senior Living Center, and organized fundraising programs for Alzheimer's awareness.

"It's never been about the title. It's never been about the crown. It's about the impact."

— Kiran Reddy

Reddy also aims to provide prenatal care to underprivileged women in developing nations, a goal she traces to watching her father's medical practice.

Carrying a Legacy Forward

Reddy's win continues a growing tradition of Indian American success in national pageants. Nina Davuluri became the first Indian American Miss America in 2013, and Reddy has spoken about carrying that legacy forward as a role model for daughters of non-white immigrants.

Her next stop is the Miss Teen Universe competition in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, on October 25, where she will represent the United States on the international stage for the first time in the pageant's history.

The $25,000 prize winner will balance her new role with her first semester at the University of Georgia, where she begins classes this fall.
